name: bug_caret_off_after_focus
description: BUG: the caret went OFF on the first tick after focus. `TextEditManager::initialize_editing` set `blink.is_visible = true` and, in the same breath, `blink.last_input_time = None`. `None` is the 'no input has EVER been recorded' encoding, for which `BlinkState::should_blink` is true IMMEDIATELY — and the blink timer has an interval but no delay, so `Timer::invoke` runs it on the very first pump. `ToggleCursorVisibility` therefore found `should_blink == true` at t≈0 and turned the caret the user had just placed straight back off; it only reappeared a full 530 ms later. Identical on X11/Wayland and headless (`process_timers_and_threads` pumps on every poll there, `Runner::pump_timers` on every service here), so this was shipped behaviour, not a harness artefact. It also made the callers responsible for repairing state `initialize_editing` had just broken: `handle_focus_change_for_cursor_blink` calls `reset_blink_on_input` BEFORE the deferred `finalize_pending_focus_changes` reaches `initialize_editing` (overwritten), `process_mouse_click_for_selection` calls it AFTER (survived), and `process_accessibility_action` never did (broken). `initialize_editing` now calls `reset_blink_on_input(Instant::now())`, which sets both halves consistently. BEAT 1 — immediately after focus the caret is ON. BEAT 2 — after a 300 ms tick, i.e. still inside the first half-period, it is STILL on: `should_blink` is false, so even when the timer does fire the caret is held solid. BEAT 3 — the counter-assertion, and the reason this is not just 'pin the caret on forever': after a further 300 ms (past CURSOR_BLINK_INTERVAL_MS = 530) the caret really does go off, in the engine flag AND in the pixels.

css: body { font-size: 24px; color: black; background: white; }
